title: K5 Fixed-Spectrum Relative-Orientation Ambiguity Audit
question: After fixing det(S)=1 and the complete eigenvalue spectrum of the conditional cycle metric, does the scaled off-support profile still depend on the orientation of S relative to physically fixed cycle probes, while remaining invariant under simultaneous co-rotation of metric and probes?
model_scope: linearized mixed Gaussian K5 surrogate with support rank 4 and cycle rank 6

construction.rotated_metric: S = R S0 R^T with nontrivial orthogonal R
construction.full_block_metric: H = [[A,C],[C^T,S + C^T A^-1 C]] so Schur(H|A)=S

positive_result_interpretation: Within this surrogate, fixing determinant and even the entire conditional-metric spectrum does not fix the finite off-support profile relative to a physically fixed probe frame. Exact co-rotation invariance shows that the residual effect is relative orientation, not a coordinate-basis artifact.
claim_lock: A PASS does not establish ambiguity of a physical EPRL/Toller amplitude, does not identify cycle coordinates as observables, and does not close D7 or NEW_REQUIRED. It only sharpens what additional geometric data a microscopic prescription would have to fix or gauge-quotient in this Gaussian K5 class.
